claim_evidence.claim_text: Four reviewed implementation cases provide enough recurring and contrasting evidence to propose bounded responsibility annotations and terminology changes, but not to establish field-wide representativeness, taxonomy saturation, mechanism effectiveness, or independent convergence.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Executive judgment; What the evidence can and cannot support
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the stated evidence boundary; low for field-wide generalization. OpenClaw/Hermes independence is mechanism-specific and unresolved outside named links.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Retain R1 as one responsibility and require lifecycle-scale and ingress-origin annotations when they materially change persistence, ownership, cancellation, retry, or completion semantics.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-001: keep R1; name lifecycle scale and ingress origin
claim_evidence.confidence: high as a four-case comparison recommendation. Scale vocabulary must remain extensible.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Retain R2, R3, and R5 as separate multi-label responsibilities: policy selection, per-call materialization, and executable action authority remain different questions even when a runtime path joins them.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-002: keep R2, R3, and R5 distinct
claim_evidence.confidence: high for analytical usefulness across the four cases; component boundaries vary.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Retain the R5/R6 boundary and trace request, authorization, execution, raw result, transformation, persistence, and model-visible observation as distinct stages where present; do not claim completeness for perception-grounded systems before the deferred Browser Use case.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-003: keep R5 and R6; trace the handoff
claim_evidence.confidence: high for symbolic tool/result paths; low for browser/GUI perception until a deep case exists.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Treat extension and policy injection as a cross-cutting dimension described by affected responsibility, lifecycle boundary, owner, authority, persistence effect, failure posture, and activation state rather than adding an extensions responsibility.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-004: treat injection as a cross-cutting dimension
claim_evidence.confidence: high across four different extension architectures; installed third-party behavior remains deployment-specific.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Retain the stable R9 identifier, rename it to “Runtime integrity, recovery, and task acceptance,” and require separate reporting of protocol/runtime integrity, operational recovery, evidence acquisition, and task verification/acceptance; keep pre-action authorization primarily in R5.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-005: keep R9 stable, but require separate operational and task contracts
claim_evidence.confidence: high that a flat R9 is misleading; moderate that internal facets are preferable to a top-level split before broader cases.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Formalize control owner as an extensible multi-value dimension and record study-object type separately; a framework or substrate exposes mechanisms while downstream applications may own the policies required by a concrete-harness case question.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-006: formalize control owner and study-object type
claim_evidence.confidence: high for multi-party ownership; framework guidance remains selection-level until a dedicated comparison.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Rename R11 to “Across-run adaptation,” describe the changed artifact, trigger, signal, authority, and retention rule, and reserve “outcome-driven optimization” for a demonstrated loop in which measured outcomes select future changes.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-007: rename R11 around adaptation; earn the word optimization
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the conceptual distinction; only OpenClaw and Hermes show positive adaptation, and their mechanism-level independence is unresolved. No case demonstrates outcome optimization.

claim_evidence.claim_text: When a material claim uses “default,” record applicable surface or entry point, activation state, and—where relevant—configuration origin, migration generation, explicit override, and effective runtime value.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for Hermes's population split; moderate for generality because only one case contains the full migration shape.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Record lineage and evidentiary independence per mechanism or finding, distinguishing direct port, translated compatibility, documented inspiration, shared source, unresolved similarity, and no known link; no known link is not proof of independent development.
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the OpenClaw/Hermes relationship; broader vocabulary should remain extensible.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Retain R10 but report operational observability and external evaluation separately, because traces, events, tests, and cost records do not themselves establish task success or mechanism effectiveness.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: TF-010: observability is not external evaluation
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the four inspected boundaries; private evaluation systems remain unknowable.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Adopt static-first implementation analysis with focused upstream test execution only for a predeclared load-bearing ambiguity, in a disposable writable copy at the exact pin, with narrow interpretation and full environment disclosure; do not require full upstream suites for routine case promotion.
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate-high as a proportional-evidence policy. Test execution establishes only the selected behavior in the recorded environment, not outcome effectiveness.

claim_evidence.claim_text: The first synthesis should teach where harnesses place control by comparing model-directed loops inside programmed execution and recovery envelopes, with runtime integrity versus task acceptance as the central distinction.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Recommended first synthesis and learning chapter
claim_evidence.confidence: high for learning value from the reviewed cases; it remains a proposed narrative, not an effectiveness claim.

claim_evidence.claim_text: The current four-case batch cannot assess whether its R5/R6 distinctions transfer to perception-grounded browser or GUI paths, and it also lacks reviewed closed-production and framework/substrate cases; one Browser Use case can test transfer but cannot establish a complete action/observation taxonomy or representative field coverage.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Recommended first synthesis and learning chapter; evidence limits
claim_evidence.confidence: high that the gaps exist; their eventual effect on the proposed lens is unknown.

claim_evidence.claim_text: All four reviewed cases place a model-directed choice loop inside programmed execution, state, integrity, and recovery envelopes, while differing in where those envelopes begin and whether task acceptance is default, optional, conditioned, or external.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: The recurring architecture underneath the products
claim_evidence.confidence: high for the four pinned case boundaries; this is recurrence, not effectiveness or field prevalence, and OpenClaw/Hermes are not independent evidence where lineage is unresolved.

claim_evidence.claim_text: Browser Use at the approved pin is the strongest already-admitted post-learning falsification case because it directly tests the batch's unreviewed perception-grounded action/observation boundary; this is a sampling recommendation, not a claim that one case closes the gap.
claim_evidence.artifact_location: Recommended first synthesis and learning chapter; Gate B decision requested
claim_evidence.confidence: moderate as a next-case judgment; the maintainer may prioritize a different gap after reading the first learning experience.
